videos.title: Why the Lemur Has Eyes That Glow in the Dark #Shorts

comments.author: @GracieNJavie
comments.text: If you've ever been in a dense forest at dusk, you know that as the sun goes down, it approaches near total black out faster than the setting sun.
comments.replyText: Exactly. That rapid blackout in a forest at dusk is exactly why the tapetum lucidum is so critical. Without it, a lemur foraging at twilight would be navigating blind through branches at speed. That mirror layer is the difference between finding food and becoming it. Really appreciate you sharing that perspective.

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Every photon gets two chances to be detected
clipCandidates.why: Biological mirror bounces light back through eye twice — high curiosity density
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: A lemur's eyes have a mirror behind the retina
